message.reasoning:
need to process orders and statement.

Order: PED-1010 amount 80.00, expires_at 2026-09-10T10:00:00-03:00.

Statement lines:

1. e2e_id E1000000010001, payment, amount 80.00, time 09:00 -03:00, txid PED-1010.
2. e2e_id E1000000010002, payment, amount 80.00, time 09:02 -03:00, txid PED-1010.
3. e2e_id E1000000010003, refund, amount -80.00, time 12:00 -03:00, refers_to E1000000010002, txid null.

Rule 1: each e2e_id distinct; none duplicate. So both payments count.

Link payment to order by txid (present). Both payments link to PED-1010.

Refund line: belongs to a payment (refers_to). Refund line is not orphan.

Now compute status. Need to consider all distinct transfers linked to order: includes both payment lines and refund line? Payments list includes refund lines too. However status uses gross amount received in payment lines; a partial refund is not subtracted (rule 11). Refunds don't affect gross amount, but rule 8: order is refunded only when refunds linked to it add up to exactly the total of its linked payments. Here refunds: one refund of -80.00 linked to payment E1000000010002. Total of linked payments: we have two payments each 80 = 160 gross. Refund amount total = 80 (absolute). Not equal to total payments (160). So not fully refunded. Not "refunded".

Now compute amount received: sum of distinct payment amounts = 80 + 80 = 160.

Compare to order amount 80. Received > order amount => overpaid. Also need to see if any late condition: rule 12: when several transfers linked, compare time of latest one with expires_at. Latest payment is at 09:02, which is before expires 10:00 → on time. Overpaid status takes precedence before late_paid? Order of status precedence: unpaid, refunded, underpaid, overpaid, late_paid, paid. So overpaid applies earlier than late_paid and paid. So status = "overpaid".

Now payments list: distinct e2e_ids linked to order, including refund lines, sorted. Sorted lexicographically? Likely alphanumeric ascending. So e2e_ids: "E1000000010001", "E1000000010002", "E1000000010003". Include refund line too.

Orphans: distinct e2e_ids of payment lines not linked to any order. All payment lines are linked, so none. Orphans list empty.

Now produce JSON.

{
 "orders": {
   "PED-1010": {
     "status": "overpaid",
     "payments": ["E1000000010001","E1000000010002","E1000000010003"]
   }
 },
 "orphans": []
}

Make sure formatting matches: keys sorted? Not required. Use JSON code block.
